summary: The University of Twente Scholarship gives non-EU master's students between €3,000 and €22,000 for the first year, and the same amount in the second year if they keep their grades up. It is for students in the best 5 to 10% of their graduating class who are admitted to one of more than 30 master's programmes. The form closes on 1 April 2027.
meta_description: The University of Twente Scholarship gives non-EU master's students €3,000 to €22,000 a year. Admission first, then the form by 1 April 2027.
covers: €3,000 to €22,000 for the first year, as a contribution to study costs. Nothing, including tuition, is paid on your behalf.
The same amount in the second year of a two-year master's, if you meet the progress rules.
eligibility: Non-EU/EEA students who are not eligible for Dutch student finance and have not graduated from Twente before.
Among the best 5 to 10% of your graduating class.

Provisional admission to a participating master's starting in September 2027 (more than 30, including Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Psychology and Business Administration). ITC master's and pre-master's are excluded.
IELTS Academic 6.5 with speaking 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 90 with speaking 20.
how_to_apply: Apply for your master's first; you need the student number Twente gives you.
Fill in the scholarship form with your student number. It opened on 15 October 2026 at 09:00 CET and closes on 1 April 2027 at 16:00 CET.
Results are announced in the first week of May 2027.
watch_out: It is not a full scholarship or a tuition waiver: make sure you can pay the rest.
For the second-year payment you need an average of 7 out of 10 and at least 50% of first-year credits by the end of the third quartile.
UTS winners can also apply for Twente's Kipaji Scholarship, which has its own conditions.
documents: A master's application and Twente student number

faq.q: How much is the University of Twente Scholarship?
faq.a: Between €3,000 and €22,000 for the first year, with the same amount possible in the second year.
1 April 2027 at 16:00 CET for programmes starting in September 2027.
Non-EU/EEA students in the best 5 to 10% of their class, admitted to a participating master's.
